text:
The city’s electric hum died, replaced by the sudden, heavy silence of a held breath. On the rooftop, the blackout wasn’t an absence but a revelation. The solar-powered fairy lights, usually drowned out by neon glare, now pulsed like bioluminescent veins against the dark sky. Without the streetlamps’ orange haze, the stars erupted with violent clarity, mirroring the garden’s dormant seeds waiting for dawn.

A fox, bold in the darkness, trotted past the raised beds, its eyes reflecting the faint glow of moonlit kale. The wind carried the scent of damp earth and jasmine, unfiltered by exhaust fumes. In the valley below, skyscrapers stood as black monoliths, windows dead to the world. Yet here, above the grid, life thrived in the void. The garden became a sanctuary where time slowed, measured not by clock towers but by the rhythmic opening of night-blooming cereus flowers, their white petals unfolding like silent explosions in the velvet dark.
